控制整个界面，ops 按顺序执行。界面按标签页组织。工作状态（底栏上切换，见 s:
Control the whole interface; ops run in order. The interface is organized in tabs. A workspace (switched in the status bar; see workspace in screen) only decides one set of windows; the sidebar is independent of it and is only for browsing and opening tabs, and changing its list doesn't move windows; the same panel (the Tutor, say) can appear in several workspaces at once. The operations below all act on the workspace this conversation is in; if the learner has switched away, they still land there, and a dot lights up on its tab in the status bar.
- open: open a panel. panel is chat (give agent: tutor for the Tutor / flash for Quick answer), file (give path), map (topic optional), journal, review (review due cards), library (the card library), memory (Memory: stages, due forecast, review history), noteinfo (the outline, backlinks, outgoing links and tags beside a note), skills (the skill store), settings, home, web (give url: open a web page or PDF in the reader on the learner's side, read as text, with clickable links, without jumping to a browser); where is left / right / top / bottom (a split next to the panel given in to), float, or tab (the default: put it in the tab group that to is in; without to, in the most recently used group on the same side).
- close / focus / float: panel is a panel id or title (look in screen).
- move: move panel next to to; where as above.
- layout: replace this workspace's whole layout. spec is {"split": "h" or "v", "sizes": [0.5, 0.5], "parts": [spec, ...]}, and a leaf is {"tabs": [panel, ...]}; a panel can be an existing panel's id or an object like the one for open.
- workspace: switch to the workspace name (a name or id); you can't switch when the learner has already switched away. With new set to true, create one and switch to it: name, icon, spec (as in layout; without it, as things look now). sidebar: open false collapses the sidebar, true expands it; list changes the sidebar's list (topics, cards, notes, lessons, work, practice, files, skills), and windows don't move.
- theme: design and apply a theme (colors and style). name is the theme name (the same name changes the existing one; name “default” goes back to the default look); base is dark or light, the look to start from; vars are the color variables to change {name: CSS color}; the ones you can change are bg (window background), panel (panels), panel-hi (popups and input boxes), surface (cards and buttons), surface-hover, line, line-soft (borders), text, muted, subtle (three levels of text), accent (accent color), accent-ink (text on the accent color), accent-glow (light accent background), ai, ai-glow (the AI's color), amber, red, green, code-bg, code-text, select-bg, active-line, tk-kw / tk-str / tk-num / tk-com / tk-fn / tk-type / tk-prop / tk-op / tk-tag (code highlighting), rb0 / rb1 / rb2 (rainbow brackets), shadow and pop-shadow (full box-shadow values), veil (popup overlay); font and mono are the body and code fonts (names of fonts installed on this computer); css is extra CSS for changing style such as corner radius, shadows and spacing (url() and @import aren't allowed); note says what this theme is in one sentence; apply false only saves it without applying it; replace true replaces the colors as a whole set instead of merging; delete true deletes this theme. warnings in the result point out combinations with too little contrast to read well; keep changing until there are no warnings. The learner can go back to how it was before your change with one click.
- set: change the look; key is theme (dark / light), font_size, code_font_size, line_height, read_width (the most characters in a line, 20 to 120, or none for no limit), density (compact / comfortable); with key zoom, only the size of the one window panel is changed, and value is the factor (1.2 is 120%); line_height and read_width with panel given also change only that one window; value null restores the default.
The interface only decides what is shown; it doesn't tell you what's in the vault: to know which cards, notes, topics and practices exist, look them up with list, graph or read; don't infer it from the panels.
The learner can restore the interface as it was before your changes with one click. Don't close or move a panel they're typing in.
提出修改一个 AI 的规则（tutor 主会话、flash 快答、coach 练: Propose a change to an AI's rules (tutor for the Tutor, flash for Quick answer, coach for the Practice coach, organizer for the Organizer): the rules are the way of working it reads every turn, and the properties at the top list the tools it can use. Given only agent, it returns its current rules in full; read them before changing them. Like changing a skill, it doesn't take effect directly: the learner reviews it side by side and can keep editing, and it takes effect once approved; every change keeps its history, and the rules before and after the change can each answer once in the same conversation for comparison. content is the full changed text, or give edits ([{old, new}], each old must appear exactly once in the original); why says in one sentence why you're changing it; questions gives two or three questions that best show the effect. Keep rules short rather than long: say clearly what to achieve, don't list rule after rule.
提出修改一个技能（技能列表见系统说明的「技能」一节；先用 skill 读它现在的: Propose a change to a skill (the skill list is in the “Skills” section of the system instructions; read its current full text with skill first). It doesn't change directly: the learner sees where you changed it side by side (deletions in red, additions in green), can keep editing, switch back to the original or not use it, and it takes effect once approved; every change keeps its history. name is the skill name; file defaults to SKILL.md and can also be one of its accompanying files; give content for the full changed text (for SKILL.md you can write only the body; properties at the top that you leave out keep their old values), or give edits ([{old, new}], each old must appear exactly once in the original); why says in one sentence why you're changing it. With new set to true, it creates a skill: name is its name, and content is the complete SKILL.md (the properties at the top need name, title, description, category). questions gives two or three questions that best show the effect of this change (things the learner would really ask, short): when the learner clicks one, the skill before and after the change each answers it once for comparison.

改学习库里的一个文件：只改要改的地方，文件的其余部分不动。edits 是一处或好: Change a file in the vault: change only what needs changing and leave the rest of the file alone. edits are one or several changes [{old, new}], replaced in order; each old must appear exactly once in the file (after the earlier changes are made). why says in one sentence what this version changes and why (for example “add a temperature parameter to see how sampling changes”): it is this version's description, which the learner sees in the file's version history and can compare line by line with the previous version. Keep changing the same program in its original file; don't save it as a new file like _v2, _new or -ext.
